subject: general
question: A train 100 m long is running at a speed of 70 km per hour. In how much time will it pass a man who is running at 10 km per hour in the same direction in which the train is going?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since both are running in the same direction, Relative Speed = 70 − 10 = 60 km/hr.

Convert speed to m/sec: 60 × (5/18) = 50/3 m/sec.

Distance to be covered = Length of the train = 100 m.

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 100 ÷ (50/3) = 6 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the train = 100 m

Speed of the train = 70 km/hr

Speed of the man = 10 km/hr

Direction = Same direction

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed of Train − Speed of Object

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 70 − 10 = 60 km/hr

⇒ Speed in m/sec = 60 × (5/18) = 300/18 = 50/3 m/sec

⇒ Distance to cross the man = Length of train = 100 m

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 100 ÷ (50/3)

⇒ Time = (100 × 3) ÷ 50 = 6 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 6 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). If they move in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/sec, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/sec to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a stationary or moving point object (like a man, pole, or tree), the total distance covered is equal to the length of the train itself.
